entries.note: This is a caricature of industry optimism, without a definite empirical commitment.

entries.test: Public construction records would establish how much of the cited 61GW was actually being built in March 2026.
entries.note: The normalization drops “I don’t think,” making the conclusion firmer; the construction claim nevertheless has a plain factual reading.

entries.test: Available generation and deliverable power commitments could be compared with the power requirements of the cited 61GW of IT load.
entries.note: “They” refers to the previously discussed capacity under active development, not all planned US data centers.

entries.test: North American commissioning and operating-capacity records for 2025 would establish the new operational IT load and associated power demand.
entries.note: The approximate figures preserve the estimate’s precision.
Calling the number a disaster evaluates its significance.

entries.test: Public sales, shipment, inventory and installation disclosures could establish the value of FY2026 US NVIDIA hardware purchases remaining uninstalled.
entries.note: This is a factual estimate even if his calculation is unreliable.

entries.test: NVIDIA quarterly GPU shipments and contemporaneous deployment rates would show whether operationalizing a quarter’s sales required roughly six months.
entries.note: The surrounding calculation supplies a throughput interpretation.

entries.test: Quarterly NVIDIA GPU sales and new operational data center capacity, converted to comparable hardware capacity, would show their relative pace and sales acceleration.
Deployment records for the Blackwell purchases under discussion and Vera Rubin’s release date would establish Rubin’s age when those deployments finish.
entries.note: The installation milestone supplies an event, not a calendar deadline.

entries.test: Published project schedules, construction progress and documented delay causes would show whether build durations beyond industry representations independently explain delays.

entries.note: The normalization omits “wholly” and maintaining current revenue. The claimed exclusive dependence on persuading buyers concerns their beliefs and a counterfactual revenue path.

entries.test: Planning applications, contracts, financing records and cancellation disclosures would establish whether a concrete Abilene extension project existed.
entries.note: The plain factual core denies that there was a real extension project.

entries.test: Dated completion records for all eight Stargate Abilene buildings would show whether the whole project was completed by October 2026.
entries.note: “By October” is read as reaching completion by that month; an explicitly end-of-October deadline would still be pending.
“Feels like” expresses a suspicion of coordinated concealment; the normalization turns it into an established fact.

entries.test: Construction progress and completion records would show whether Abilene finishes in late 2027 if its March 2026 construction rate continues.

entries.note: “I imagine” explicitly marks the capacity estimate as conjecture.

entries.test: Operating-capacity records could identify an in-service gigawatt campus, while financial disclosures could establish OpenAI’s ability to meet its bills.
entries.note: His inability to find a campus is weaker than saying none can be found.
The normalization converts a sweeping insult into a specific claim about lenders’ understanding. Private-credit financing itself is factual.

entries.test: Public commissioning records or definitive project cancellations would establish whether the Nebius capacity contracted to Meta is ever built.
entries.note: The normalization drops “likely” from the three-to-four-year estimate. The separate “it’s never happening” prediction is categorical.

entries.test: Completion, cancellation and payment records for the announced deals would establish whether many projects are never built and consequently never paid.
entries.note: “I think” introduces an asserted prediction, rather than an explicit possibility.
“May never be built” identifies a possibility, not a firm project-outcome prediction.

entries.test: Project schedules, actual construction progress and loan-interest disclosures would show whether delays are extending debt-interest accrual.
Following clearance of a compute shortage, public capacity, utilization, valuation and commissioning records would establish the predicted glut, value decline and GPU age at startup.
entries.note: The normalization moves GPU age from when the data centers turn on to when the bottleneck clears.

entries.test: Operator financial statements, customer losses, construction trends and market valuation evidence would test the asserted debt burden and construction-driven valuation.
entries.note: The normalization drops “all” from unprofitability and makes an apparently decelerating boom definitively decelerating.
“Mirage” and “pipedream” supply denunciation without a definite completion or financing test for the whole claim.

entries.test: Completion and definitive cancellation records for the announced data center deals would establish whether a majority never gets built.
entries.note: He adopts the paraphrase in his own voice. The historical-waste ranking is evaluative, but the majority prediction is concrete.

entries.test: Deployment records for NVIDIA’s 2025–2026 sales and corresponding construction rates would show whether operationalization takes until 2028–2029 under the stated assumptions.
entries.note: The prediction explicitly depends on construction continuing at the cited rate and projects being built.
“Benefit to anybody involved” supplies no shared measure or bounded outcome, especially for future benefits.

entries.test: Operators’ reported revenue attributable to US capacity newly operating in 2025 would show whether it generated the asserted tens of billions.
entries.note: The normalization treats the assumed 3GW as established and shifts from publicly showing revenue to earning it.

entries.test: Public AI-compute spending, customer concentration and capacity-utilization data would establish demand levels and whether a few companies dominate purchases.
entries.note: The context gives “demand” a commercial-compute reading, and the concentration claim is concrete.

entries.test: Future reported NVIDIA GPU sales would establish whether spending declines from preceding comparable periods.
Construction-rate and completion records for the cited compute-deal projects would show whether any finish before 2030 while maintaining the referenced rate.
Project progress reports and documented critical-path delays would establish whether unrealistic construction schedules independently explain delays beyond power constraints.
entries.note: The counterfactual is an argument for an observable causal claim.

entries.test: Public NVIDIA sales records and customer deployment or inventory disclosures would establish the revenue value of chips sold but uninstalled.

entries.note: “Reasonable to believe” presents this installation horizon as a qualified expectation.
The extracted quantity comes from “I’d wager quite a few”; the separate assertion that some arrived is firm.
GPU arrivals are factual, but the combined claim speculates about Huang’s and NVIDIA’s private knowledge.
“Would not be shocked” states a possibility.

entries.test: Publicly reported employee policies, compensation criteria and production-development practices would establish the claimed AI-use requirements.
entries.note: The normalization softens “everybody” and “as much as possible” to unspecified employees using tools heavily.

entries.test: Documented internal-tool functionality and measured development time versus realized time savings would test the described outcomes.
entries.note: The source rejects treating these practices as evidence of an efficacy leap; it does not categorically establish that no leap occurred.
“Slow destruction” of the industry’s software stack lacks a shared outcome threshold.
The combined claim includes “LLMs do not think,” without a shared operational definition of thinking.

entries.test: Comparative code audits and reviewer-workflow studies would establish standards compliance, review time and resulting skimming or LLM delegation.
entries.note: The normalization weakens “rarely aligns” and omits the guaranteed increase in review time.

entries.test: Public company policies and workforce studies would show whether AI mandates across almost every major tech company reward reduced independent coding and architecture learning.
Public code audits, review records, incident analyses and staffing disclosures would show whether poorly reviewed AI code degrades systems while knowledgeable engineers are laid off.
entries.note: The metaphor has a plain operational reading about software degradation.

entries.test: Public software-quality and maintenance audits at companies rewarding token use would test whether those incentives invariably produce poor software outcomes.
entries.note: “Guaranteeing” is a strong causal assertion, not merely a concern.

entries.test: A major service’s outage reports and root-cause analysis would establish a prolonged failure caused by widespread AI coding and compounded by layoffs and busywork incentives.
entries.note: The normalization omits the busywork culture as a compounding cause. “Near future” supplies no definite deadline.
“Especially when” intensifies an unconditional crisis prediction rather than making it contingent. The normalization also turns dollar-valued usage into compute cost.

entries.test: Public longitudinal studies of engineers relying almost exclusively on LLMs for several months would establish whether they subsequently need to relearn basic job practices.
entries.note: This describes a general skill-loss effect of prolonged reliance, not a dated future cohort.
Neither the aggregate damage nor the point when it is repaired has a shared definition.
This is a demand for accountability.
The universal denunciation supplies no definite factual proposition.

entries.test: Public sales, inventory and deployment disclosures would establish whether most of the cited GPU sales by dollar value remained uninstalled.
Anthropic’s publicly disclosed historical financial results would establish cumulative revenue and salary-plus-compute expenditure over the four years discussed.
Public financial statements separating AI-compute rental revenue and costs would show whether any provider reports profits from that activity.
entries.note: “Appears” here frames the state of reported profitability, which public accounts can test.

entries.test: Public budget records, layoff explanations and task-replacement evidence would establish whether AI expenses drive engineering layoffs without AI taking over the eliminated work.
Public AI revenue figures and controlled workplace studies would test commercial revenue, tangible productivity gains and effects of mandated use.
entries.note: The categorical denial of tangible productivity benefits is testable despite the qualified harm assertion.

entries.test: Public cost studies and longitudinal or controlled assessments of AI users would establish effects on productivity, retained skills, learning and independent performance.
entries.note: The poisonous-future language is evaluative, but the claimed learning and productivity harms are empirical.
